heard: The fastest object ever launched from Earth carried a postage stamp. On January 19, 2006, NASA launched New Horizons directly into an escape trajectory. It reached an Earth-relative speed of 16.26 km per second, setting the launch record. In 2007, a Jupiter gravity assist added roughly 4 km per second of speed. Astronomers used the ALMA radio telescope, array in Chile, to precisely measure Pluto's orbit. On July 14, 2015, New Horizons became the first spacecraft to study Pluto up close. The probe flew past at over 52,000 miles per hour, carrying nine cultural mementos. Among them was a 1991 postage stamp printed with Pluto, not yet explored. After roughly 9.5 years, that probe finally delivered the stamp to its destination.
